transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-23 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Elena Ruiz (Head of Security, Summitbridge), Tom Baker (Platform Engineer), Priya Shah (Legal Counsel), Ibrahim Kahn (ML Eng)

Auto-summary (auto):
- Goal: Understand residency, key management, log retention and redaction constraints for potential pilot.
- High sensitivity: financial PII, trade secrets; need strong evidence for region locking, KMS, and audit trails.
- Primary interest: evaluate Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private deployment for production inference.

Transcript:
00:00 Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Alex from Redwood, i'm joined by Marcus and Priya from our solutions team. Can you hear us okay?
00:05 Elena Ruiz: Yes, thanks. We have about 45-ish minutes, is that right?
00:08 Alex Kim: Yep 50 minutes ish, perfect. Can we go around quickly for intro?
00:13 Tom Baker: Tom Baker, platform. We run our infra on multi-cloud, primarily GCP in eu-west.
00:18 Ibrahim Kahn: Ibrahim, ML eng, working on model infra and inference pipelines.
00:21 Priya Shah: Priya Shah, legal counsel, contracting and data privacy lead.
00:24 Alex Kim: Great, Alex Kim, AE focusing on financials. Marcus?
00:27 Marcus Lee: Marcus Lee, solutions eng, I focus on runtime and deployment patterns.
00:31 Elena Ruiz: Great. High level -- we're evaluating a few vendors. Main constraints: GDPR compliance for EEA customers, HIPAA-ish controls for some healthcare-related portfolios, and most importantly strict log retention and redaction requirements from our internal audit. So we wanted to map redwood's hosting options to those controls.
00:46 Alex Kim: Totally, that's exactly what this call is for. Before we dive, quick qualification: what's the timeline if we like what we see? Pilot in Q2, production in Q3?
00:55 Ibrahim Kahn: Yes that's the plan. Pilot Q2, likely start with hosted but open to dedicated if residency or controls require it.
01:02 Elena Ruiz: Also cost matters but not at the expense of controls. We need to know where keys live, who can access logs, and whether log scrubbing is possible before any long term retention.
01:12 Marcus Lee: Understood. To frame, Redwood offers three main paths: Hosted (our managed cloud endpoints), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in our infra with isolated tenancy), and Private (control plane deployed in your VPC or on-prem). Each has different guarantees for data residency, key management, and log access.
01:32 Alex Kim: Quick question on data classification - will the inference payloads include raw customer PII or tokenized references?
01:38 Ibrahim Kahn: A mix, some PII and some hashed identifiers. For a pilot we'll probably use hashed tokens but prod will see near-PHI in certain products.
01:46 Elena Ruiz: So we need HIPAA safe handling for that subset. Also our policy says encryption keys for PHI must be in our KMS or an HSM we control or via an escrow model.
01:56 Marcus Lee: We support a few patterns: customer-managed keys in cloud KMS for Dedicated and Private, HSM integration on Private, and bring-your-own-key (BYOK) with limited escrow for Dedicated & Private. On Hosted we have a managed KMS but we do offer CMEK options in some regions — caveat is for strict HSM-only policies we usually recommend Private.
02:15 Priya Shah: When you say 'managed KMS' on Hosted, who has access to the master keys?
02:19 Marcus Lee: Short answer: Redwood does hold the service key in certain Hosted configurations; access is audited and limited, but we get requests for stronger controls. For Dedicated/Private you can control the key. We'll send the KMS integration matrix after.
02:31 Elena Ruiz: We'll want that matrix and proof points. SOC2? ISO? Pen test reports?
02:35 Alex Kim: Yes, SOC2 Type II, ISO 27001, and pen test summary available. We'll share the evidence pack.
02:40 Elena Ruiz: Good.
02:42 Tom Baker: On residency, our requirement is strict region locking: all inference requests for EU customers need to stay within eu-west and logs must not cross to US or other regions.
02:52 Marcus Lee: For Dedicated we can pin model serving nodes to a region and disable cross-region fallback. For Hosted there is routing by region but automatic fallback may cross regions unless we lock it. We can set routing policies to prioritize eu nodes and disable cross-region fallback for strict scenarios, but some enterprise features require Dedicated or Private for absolute guarantees.
03:11 Elena Ruiz: Can you explain more about logs: what exact logs are captured? Are inference prompts stored long term?
03:18 Marcus Lee: We capture request/response logs for debugging and monitoring by default, with configurable retention. For sensitive customers we offer log minimization — for Dedicated and Private you can disable retention or set short retention windows, and we support on-the-fly redaction rules for known PII patterns. For Hosted, we have sanitized logs and retention tiers but there are limits.
03:36 Ibrahim Kahn: How deterministic is redaction? We need to ensure PHI is removed before any durable storage.
03:42 Marcus Lee: Redaction runs in the request processing pipeline — it's best-effort, regex and ML-based scrubbing. For guaranteed removal we recommend Private so you control the pre-storage hooks, or Dedicated with a redaction proxy in your network path. We'll note that regex may miss edge cases, so customers with strict legal needs often prefer Private.
03:59 Priya Shah: Also we need an immutable audit trail for access to logs and keys, with retention for 7 years for certain records. Is that feasible?
04:07 Alex Kim: Yes we support audit logging and can export to your SIEM; retention policies are configurable especially for Dedicated/Private. Hosted supports exports but long term retention beyond default tiers is either an add-on or requires Dedicated.
04:17 Elena Ruiz: A concrete worry — who within Redwood can access raw inference payloads? We need role based limits and just-in-time access, ideally no human access unless approved.
04:28 Marcus Lee: Access is RBAC enforced. For Hosted, support can request access through an approval workflow and actions are logged. For Dedicated/Private you can disable vendor access entirely or require SAML-based just-in-time authorization.
04:40 Elena Ruiz: Okay, good. Another question — data residency for backups and snapshots. Does Redwood replicate model caches or checkpoint snapshots outside region?
04:48 Marcus Lee: Model binaries and caches are stored regionally when you select a regional deployment. However some global control plane metadata may be replicated; for Private the control plane sits in your VPC, so no replication. For Dedicated we provide tenancy in selected regions and can avoid cross-region replication on request.
05:02 Tom Baker: What about KV cache — we saw mention of 'kv cache' in docs. Does that persist PII?
05:07 Marcus Lee: The KV cache holds recent token state for autoregressive models; it's ephemeral by design and generally not persisted to long-term storage. Still, we treat it as in-memory sensitive. For extra caution we can flush or disable KV caching for certain routes.
05:19 Ibrahim Kahn: Any differences in inference latency if we disable KV cache or redaction? Need to know performance tradeoffs.
05:25 Marcus Lee: Yes disabling KV cache increases per-token compute cost and latency, but you can use aggressive batching to mitigate. Redaction adds a small CPU overhead pre-storage; we can quantify for your workload in a benchmark.
05:37 Alex Kim: Quick qualification: which models are you planning to serve — open models or proprietary finetunes?
05:42 Ibrahim Kahn: Mostly open-source base models with our fine-tuned heads; some workflows will push client PII into prompts though.
05:48 Elena Ruiz: We also need to ensure outputs are not used to train vendor models. Is there a SLA around 'no training on customer data'?
05:55 Marcus Lee: Redwood has a no-training-on-customer-data policy by default for Hosted customers who opt-out of data collection; Dedicated/Private customers can ensure telemetry is disabled entirely. We'll include the explicit data usage policy in the materials we send.
06:05 Priya Shah: On breach notification timelines — we need 72 hours notice for material incidents and a point of contact.
06:11 Alex Kim: Standard incident response aligns with that; we'll provide contacts and runbook excerpts.
06:15 Elena Ruiz: Great. Now on to legal hold and e-discovery: sometimes regulators ask for bulk logs. How do you ensure we can produce logs without exposing other tenants?
06:25 Marcus Lee: Logs are segregated by tenant ID. For Hosted, exports come from a service interface keyed to your tenant; we can produce redacted exports if needed. For Dedicated/Private, you control storage and access which simplifies e-discovery.
06:36 Tom Baker: Network topology question — if we go Dedicated, do we get IP allowlists and VPC peering options?
06:42 Marcus Lee: Yes Dedicated supports static IP ranges, VPC peering, and in some cases private links to cloud providers. Private is the only option for full on-prem or air-gapped.
06:50 Elena Ruiz: On the audit piece — is there a way to get on-demand snapshots of audit logs for our internal compliance team?
06:56 Marcus Lee: Yes, audit logs can be exported via S3, Kafka, or SIEM connectors. We can configure push or pull and retention per your policy.
07:04 Ibrahim Kahn: For the pilot we plan to run synthetic and low-PHI traffic. For production we need to support throughput of about 600 req/s peak and 30ms median token latency target.
07:14 Marcus Lee: That throughput is feasible on Dedicated; for Hosted you'd need to work with us for reserved capacity or we may recommend Dedicated for predictable SLOs. We'll propose a configuration.
07:22 Elena Ruiz: Costs aside, do you have references from other financial institutions who have similar residency and key custody needs?
07:28 Alex Kim: Yes we can share anonymized case studies and contactable references under an NDA. We'll include that.
07:33 Priya Shah: Any legal constraints around log redaction proving? We may need an attestation that redaction rules were applied prior to long term storage.
07:41 Marcus Lee: We can produce processing evidence: timestamps showing redaction step completed, and hashes of the original payload if you want a verifiable chain — though storing hashes of raw payloads may itself be sensitive. For highest assurance customers we advise Private so you run the redaction step inside your network.
07:57 Tom Baker: A technical nit — how do you handle model rollouts and versions? If we pin a model version, does that affect residency or cache placement?
08:05 Marcus Lee: You can pin versions; rollout metadata is part of the control plane. Model binaries are stored in the selected region for each pinned version. Cache placement follows the serving nodes.
08:13 Elena Ruiz: Okay, thanks. Quick question about access controls for customer engineers: can we integrate SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning?
08:21 Marcus Lee: Yes SSO SAML and SCIM provisioning supported across all deployment modes, with role mapping. For Hosted we manage the IdP integration; for Dedicated/Private you can host your own.
08:30 Ibrahim Kahn: Any rate-limiting or quota controls we can expose to internal teams? We want fine-grained per-route quotas.
08:36 Marcus Lee: Yes, per-route quotas, token caps, and throttles are available. Dedicated includes higher limits and more granular control.
08:42 Elena Ruiz: Let's talk about a hypothetical: a subpoena requires us to hand over inference logs for a EU user. We need to ensure the logs handed over are complete and provenance is intact. How do you support chain-of-custody?
08:55 Marcus Lee: Audit logs include request IDs, timestamps, tenantID and access logs. We can provide export packages with manifest files and signed checksums. For legal-sensitive deliveries, customers often run exports from their Private control plane to maintain custody.
09:10 Priya Shah: Good. Any limitations on encryption in transit between Redwood and data sources?
09:15 Marcus Lee: TLS 1.2+ enforced; mutual TLS available for Dedicated/private network peering.
09:20 Alex Kim: I want to surface a couple of gotchas we've seen: hosted fallbacks can be turned off but sometimes customers forget; and redaction relying only on regex can be brittle.
09:29 Elena Ruiz: We'll treat those as blockers unless mitigated.
09:32 Alex Kim: Understood. Quick pricing ask: can you ballpark Dedicated committed cost for 600 req/s and 30ms?
09:39 Marcus Lee: We'll take that offline and run a capacity estimate; i'll add it to the action items.
09:42 Elena Ruiz: Ok. We're nearing the end — any gaps we haven't covered?
09:46 Tom Baker: One more on backups: can we configure encrypt-at-rest keys per-region?
09:50 Marcus Lee: Yes region-specific CMEK supported on Dedicated and Private. Hosted has region options but keys may be service-managed unless CMEK is enabled.
09:59 Ibrahim Kahn: Also curious about telemetry — can we disable model telemetry that contains prompt data?
10:03 Marcus Lee: Yes telemetry toggles are available; Dedicated/Private have strict toggles to disable telemetry and anonymize traces.
10:11 Alex Kim: Great. Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
10:15 Alex Kim: Recap: Redwood to share SOC2/ISO evidence, KMS integration matrix, routing and region isolation diagram, and hosted vs dedicated pricing. Marcus will add notes on KV cache behavior and redaction limitations. Ibrahim will send sample payloads. We'll schedule a technical deep-dive on KMS/HSM next week.
10:31 Elena Ruiz: Sounds good. Priya Shah and I will review the materials and come back with any contract-level asks.
10:36 Alex Kim: Perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and calendar invite for the deep-dive.

End of transcript.

References/links mentioned: SOC2 / ISO evidence (link shared post-call), hosted-vs-dedicated-pricing-sheet (to be shared), KMS-integration-matrix (to be attached).
